title: Canonical constant-coefficient strict-fibre stalk comparison
statement: Let f:X→Y be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes, s:Spec Ω→Y a geometric point, Λ a commutative ring, and M a Λ-module. Use the small etale sites and their constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Let Z=X×_Y Y_(s), where Y_(s) is the strict henselization with its structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], and let η:M_Y→f_*f^*M_Y be the adjunction unit. For any lift t of s to the identity etale object Y, there exists an isomorphism r:(f_*f^*M_Y)_s→M_Z(Z). Its composite with η_s and the coefficient germ M→(M_Y)_s is exactly the canonical coefficient map M→M_Z(Z). No connectedness, integral, normal or proper hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Apply exists_qcqsStrictLocalModuleComparison to f^* M_Y in the adopted full strictLocalizationToBase presentation. Its isomorphism Theta identifies (f_* f^* M_Y)_s with global sections of p^* f^* M_Y on Z, and its representative germ formula is the actual second adjunction unit followed by the strict-local neighbourhood section. The canonical small/full colimit isomorphism identifies this presentation over Y with the strict henselization in the mathematical statement.

proof.text: Use upperStarConstantSheafIso first for f and then for p, and the canonical global-section/terminal-evaluation isomorphism. Composing their images with Theta constructs the invertible map r to sections of M_Z.

proof.text: Choose any representative affine pointed neighbourhood. Its marked point maps to t on the identity etale object because the point fibre of a terminal object is a singleton. Naturality of sheafification and of the germ maps expresses the terminal constant coefficient germ on this representative.

proof.text: Apply the defining germ formula for Theta and naturality of the first adjunction unit. The resulting expression is the first unit, the second unit, restriction along the limit leg, and the two constant-pullback comparisons. Naturality moves the first constant comparison through restriction and the second unit. The constantModuleTransition_generators equation, proved from uniqueness of left adjoints in the cited functoriality module, applies successively to f and p; naturality of sheafification along the limit leg leaves precisely the coefficient section on Z.

lean.statement: theorem constant_strict_fibre_stalk_comparison (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (t : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale s).fiber.obj (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y))) : let Φ := Scheme.pointSmallEtale s let Z := pullback f (Scheme.strictLocalizationToBase s) let F := (constantSheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M let η := (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).unit.app F ∃ r : Φ.sheafFiber.obj ((lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).obj ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).obj F)) ⟶ ((constantSheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M).obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Z))), IsIso r ∧ (toSheafify Y.smallEtaleTopology ((Functor.const Y.Etaleᵒᵖ).obj M)).app (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y))) ≫ Φ.toPresheafFiber (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y)) t F.obj ≫ Φ.sheafFiber.map η ≫ r = (toSheafify Z.smallEtaleTopology ((Functor.const Z.Etaleᵒᵖ).obj M)).app (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Z)))
